seoul-culture-first-visit.seoTitle: First Seoul Culture Day: Deoksugung, Seoul Forest or Ceramics
seoul-culture-first-visit.seoDescription: Pick one cultural anchor for a Seoul day: Deoksugung with an English palace tour, Seoul Forest gardens or Korean ceramics indoors. Get a plan you can change.

gyeongbokgung-palace-guide.seoTitle: Gyeongbokgung Palace: Tickets, Hours, Guard Ceremony and Route
gyeongbokgung-palace-guide.seoDescription: Gyeongbokgung closes Tuesdays; adults pay 3,000 won, free in hanbok, and the guard changing ceremony runs at 10:00 and 14:00. Get a three-hour route.

changdeokgung-huwon-secret-garden.seoTitle: Changdeokgung Secret Garden: Huwon Tour Booking, Times, Fees
changdeokgung-huwon-secret-garden.seoDescription: English Huwon tours run at 10:30, 11:30 and 14:30, plus 15:30 Mar to Nov; book online six days ahead or on site from 09:00. Get fees, closing day and a route.

seoul-five-grand-palaces-compared.seoTitle: Five Grand Palaces of Seoul Compared: Fees, Closing Days, Pass
seoul-five-grand-palaces-compared.seoDescription: Gyeongbokgung closes Tuesdays, the other four palaces Mondays; Deoksugung and Changgyeonggung open to 21:00. Compare fees, the 6,000-won pass and day plans.

jongmyo-shrine-guide.seoTitle: Jongmyo Shrine: Tour Days, Tickets, Royal Rite and Etiquette
jongmyo-shrine-guide.seoDescription: Jongmyo closes Tuesdays and is guided-tour only Mondays, Thursdays and Fridays, with English tours at 10:00, 12:00, 14:00 and 16:00. Get fees and rite dates.

hanbok-rental-palace-guide.seoTitle: Hanbok Rental in Seoul: Free Palace Entry Rules and Etiquette
hanbok-rental-palace-guide.seoDescription: For free palace entry in hanbok, wear a wrap-collar jeogori with a separate skirt or trousers. Learn how Seoul rental shops work and how to time the rental.

seoul-buddhist-temples-templestay.seoTitle: Seoul Buddhist Temples: Jogyesa, Bongeunsa and Templestay
seoul-buddhist-temples-templestay.seoDescription: Jogyesa and Bongeunsa are free; enter halls by the side doors with shoes off. Learn about the Lotus Lantern Festival and which Templestay format suits you.

jjimjilbang-etiquette-guide.seoTitle: Jjimjilbang Etiquette: Korean Bathhouse Rules, Nudity, Tattoos
jjimjilbang-etiquette-guide.seoDescription: Bath areas are single-sex and fully nude; the jjimjil floor is co-ed in a provided T-shirt and shorts. Get the Korean bathhouse routine, step by step.

korean-etiquette-for-visitors.seoTitle: Korean Etiquette for Tourists: Bowing, Shoes, Tipping, Subway
korean-etiquette-for-visitors.seoDescription: Korean manners for visitors come down to polite speech, a small bow, two hands, shoes off and a quiet subway. Do not tip. Get the short list that matters.

korean-table-manners.seoTitle: Korean Table Manners: Chopsticks, Banchan, Elders and Paying
korean-table-manners.seoDescription: Never leave chopsticks upright in rice, share the banchan, let the eldest start and pay at the counter; no tipping. Get Korean dining etiquette, with reasons.

gwangjang-market-food-guide.seoTitle: Gwangjang Market Food Guide: What to Eat, How to Order, Hours
gwangjang-market-food-guide.seoDescription: The Gwangjang Market food alley runs 09:00 to 23:00 daily; start with mayak gimbap and bindaetteok. Learn counter-stall ordering, cash tips and timing.

korean-bbq-ordering-guide.seoTitle: Korean BBQ: How to Order, Portions, Pork vs Beef and Grilling
korean-bbq-ordering-guide.seoDescription: Korean barbecue is ordered by the portion (inbun), usually two to start; compare meat by price per 100 g. Get pork vs beef cuts, ssam and a sample order.

makgeolli-soju-traditional-liquor.seoTitle: Makgeolli and Soju: Korean Liquor Types and Pouring Etiquette
makgeolli-soju-traditional-liquor.seoDescription: Makgeolli is unfiltered rice wine; distill the brew and you get soju. You can drink from January 1 of the year you turn 19. Learn Korean drinking etiquette.

national-museum-of-korea-guide.seoTitle: National Museum of Korea: What to See in 3 Hours and Closures
national-museum-of-korea-guide.seoDescription: Permanent galleries are free; six galleries and the Room of Senses are closed until January 28, 2027. Get a 3-hour route past the pensive bodhisattvas.

national-folk-museum-of-korea-guide.seoTitle: National Folk Museum of Korea: Free Entry, Hours, What's Open
national-folk-museum-of-korea-guide.seoDescription: The free folk museum inside Gyeongbokgung opens on Tuesdays; Hall 1 is closed until December 21, 2026. Get a plan for Halls 2 and 3 and the 1970s street.

korean-traditional-performances-seoul.seoTitle: Korean Traditional Performances in Seoul: Gugak and Pansori
korean-traditional-performances-seoul.seoDescription: Start with the Saturday Gugak Concert: 15:00, 20,000 to 30,000 won, book online by 18:00 the day before. Learn which shows need no Korean and when to clap.

korean-tea-culture-seoul.seoTitle: Korean Tea Culture in Seoul: Teahouses, Darye and Green Tea
korean-tea-culture-seoul.seoDescription: In Korea, cha means leaf tea but also yuja, omija or jujube drinks. Learn darye etiquette, how a traditional teahouse works and how to buy leaf tea.

bukchon-hanok-village-guide.seoTitle: Bukchon Hanok Village: Red Zone Hours, Fines and Etiquette
bukchon-hanok-village-guide.seoDescription: Tourists may be in the Bukchon red zone only 10:00 to 17:00; ignore a warning and you can be fined KRW 100,000. Entry is free. Get etiquette and a route.

insadong-ikseondong-guide.seoTitle: Insadong and Ikseon-dong Walk: Crafts, Hanji, Galleries, Hanok
insadong-ikseondong-guide.seoDescription: Walk Insadong-gil from Naminsa Madang to Buginsa Madang, then the 1920s hanok of Ikseon-dong, in about 3.5 hours. Learn to tell real craft from souvenirs.

seochon-neighborhood-walk.seoTitle: Seochon Walk: Tongin Market Coin Lunchbox, Museums, Inwangsan
seochon-neighborhood-walk.seoDescription: Seochon lies west of Gyeongbokgung: build a coin lunchbox at Tongin Market, walk to Suseongdong valley and skip Mondays. Get a half-day walking route.

namsangol-hanok-village-namsan.seoTitle: Namsangol Hanok Village: Free Entry, Hours and Ways Up Namsan
namsangol-hanok-village-namsan.seoDescription: Namsangol Hanok Village is free and open Tuesday to Sunday from 9:00, near Chungmuro Station. Then pick a route up to N Seoul Tower: walk, bus or cable car.

seoul-subway-tmoney-guide.seoTitle: T-money and Seoul Subway: Fares, Climate Card, Transfers
seoul-subway-tmoney-guide.seoDescription: Buy a T-money card for about 3,000 won and tap it at every gate and on every bus. The adult subway fare is 1,550 won. Learn when a Climate Card pays off.

naver-map-kakao-map-korea.seoTitle: Naver Map vs Kakao Map in Korea: English and Hangul Search
naver-map-kakao-map-korea.seoDescription: Google Maps in Korea gives no turn-by-turn walking directions, so install Naver Map, set it to English and search in Hangul. Get tips that find places fast.

korean-holidays-seollal-chuseok-travel.seoTitle: Seollal and Chuseok 2027: Holiday Dates, What Closes in Seoul
korean-holidays-seollal-chuseok-travel.seoDescription: Seollal 2027 is Sunday, Feb 7 (holiday Feb 6 to 9); Chuseok is Wednesday, Sep 15 (Sep 14 to 16). See what closes and how to plan Korean holiday travel.

korean-phrases-for-cultural-visits.seoTitle: Korean Phrases for Travelers: Palaces, Restaurants and Temples
korean-phrases-for-cultural-visits.seoDescription: Learn the polite -yo ending, juseyo (please give me) and jeogiyo (excuse me), and save 112, 119 and 1330. Get Korean phrases for tickets, ordering and taxis.

seoul-culture-itinerary-3-days.seoTitle: Seoul 3-Day Itinerary: Palaces, Secret Garden, Market, Museum
seoul-culture-itinerary-3-days.seoDescription: Day 1 Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon and Insadong; Day 2 Secret Garden, Jongmyo and Gwangjang Market; Day 3 National Museum and Namsan, ordered around closing days.

seoul-culture-by-season.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Seoul Palaces: Hours and Night Openings
seoul-culture-by-season.seoDescription: Late April to May and the second half of October suit Seoul palace gardens best. See seasonal hours, night openings, monsoon weeks and holiday closures.

seoul-indoor-culture-rainy-day.seoTitle: Rainy Day in Seoul: Indoor Museums, Teahouses, Shows, Markets
seoul-indoor-culture-rainy-day.seoDescription: On a rainy day, go to the free National Museum of Korea, reached underground from Ichon Station, or the museums at Gyeongbokgung. Get indoor swaps by area.

free-korean-culture-seoul.seoTitle: Free Things to Do in Seoul: Palaces, Museums, Guard Ceremonies
free-korean-culture-seoul.seoDescription: Every Wednesday, Changdeokgung halls, Changgyeonggung, Deoksugung and Jongmyo are free, not Gyeongbokgung or the Secret Garden. Get a free culture day plan.

korean-menu-decoder.seoTitle: Korean Menu Guide: Dish Names, Portions, Spice and Allergens
korean-menu-decoder.seoDescription: Most Korean dish names are an ingredient plus a cooking method, like gui for grilled. Learn portion words, spice cues and hidden seafood on a Korean menu.

k-drama-filming-locations-seoul.seoTitle: K-Drama Filming Locations in Seoul: Walks, Map Names, Etiquette
k-drama-filming-locations-seoul.seoDescription: Visit Seoul's K-drama filming spots by area, with the Hangul names to search in Naver Map, the dramas each place appeared in and how to visit residential lanes.

korean-street-food-guide.seoTitle: Korean Street Food in Seoul: Snacks, Markets and How to Order
korean-street-food-guide.seoDescription: Tteokbokki, eomuk, hotteok, bungeoppang and more explained, with where street food clusters in Seoul, how stalls work, paying, spice and dietary tips.

dmz-tour-from-seoul.seoTitle: DMZ Tour from Seoul: JSA Status, Paju Sites and How to Book
dmz-tour-from-seoul.seoDescription: JSA tours remain suspended; here is what you can still see on a DMZ day trip from Seoul: Imjingak, Dora Observatory and the Third Tunnel, with booking rules.
